dedupe_keys.name: capp peac energy information system sie electricity sector indicators of the central african power pool countries 2010 onwards

description: The energy information system (SIE) of the Central African Power Pool (CAPP, in French PEAC) is a web GIS and indicator platform built under an EU-funded technical assistance mission for the power pool's secretariat in Brazzaville. Its country indicators tool lets a user pick one of ten member countries (Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, DR Congo, Sao Tome and Principe, Chad) and a year from 2010 to 2026, then tick indicator groups: primary energy resources, electricity consumption, installed and available capacity of utilities, independent producers and self-consumers, generation by the same groups, imports and exports, transmission, customers, and electrical, environmental, commercial, human resources, socio-economic and generation indicators. The platform also describes a map of the existing and projected transmission network, which returned HTTP 404 from the cloud on 2026-09-28. Format and access: interactive web tables, free, no registration for the indicators; a login exists for contributors. Licence: not stated; the legal notice disclaims accuracy, completeness and timeliness. Caveats: which years are actually filled was not checked, and the data are supplied by member countries. Simulation uses: regional capacity, generation and cross-border exchange baselines for power pool planning and interconnection studies. Related records: complements the AUDA-NEPAD African Infrastructure Database.
